key_insight: A backward-mapping, genome-guided workflow can translate device-level targets into interpretable chemical design rules to discover phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The framework narrows a 13,088-composition chemical space to DFT-validated candidates, offering a practical inverse-design route for safer halide materials in optoelectronic devices.
method: Geometric formability filtering on charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions
Six-family chemical-genome descriptors plus evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates
SHAP interpretation and DFT closure for stability, band gaps, and transport/optical validation
evidence_signal: From 13,088 candidate compositions, the pipeline reduced the set to seven DFT-validated double perovskites with verified structure, band-edge character, effective masses, dielectric response, absorption, and XRD fingerprints.
watch_item: The workflow depends on surrogate models and scalar-relativistic PBE/DFT labels, so transferability to experimental synthesis and more accurate many-body electronic structure may need additional validation.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
